Six days ago, Apple released the first developer beta of iOS 27.2, skipping the iOS 27.1 beta. After releasing the second developer beta yesterday, Apple has now rolled out the first public beta of iOS 27.2, which includes a brand-new iPhone Health app. Apple has also enabled the ability to schedule and pay for lab tests through Quest Diagnostics within the new Health app.

iOS 27.2 beta includes new Health app and more

iOS 27.2 is the version following the official release of iOS 27 on September 14. iOS 27.1 is designed for iPhone Duo.

Apple has detailed how the iOS 27.1 SDK lets developers take full advantage of the iPhone Duo display. You can see here how apps look on iPhone Duo, depending on which version of iOS they target.

Apple released Xcode 27.1 beta on Friday, adding an iPhone Duo simulator and providing app development support for this all-new foldable iPhone.

The first developer beta of iOS 27.2 includes the following changes:

  • The redesigned Health app, first announced at the iPhone 18 Pro launch event, is now available in this beta.
  • Dual-camera shooting mode has been added to Group FaceTime.
  • Siri AI language support now adds French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.
  • Apple TV app profile feature lands on iPhone.
  • In Apple Podcasts, "Up Next" has been renamed to "Latest Episodes." The "Continue Playing" section now appears directly below "Latest Episodes." Episode lists in Podcasts have also been given a background that matches the theme color.
  • Apple Music now uses less icon color to mark category tabs within the app.

iOS 27.2 is expected to officially release in October. iPhone users can now get an early look at the all-new Apple Health app through the developer beta or public beta channels.
